scope.required_envelope: clean cruise through sequential flameout, loss or degradation of automatic control, transonic acceleration, stall/post-stall high angle of attack, and impact-proximate descent

admission.plain_blocker: No located public, legally redistributable candidate provides B777-200ER/Trent 892B lift, drag, moments, control effectiveness, running and windmilling-engine forces, and control-mode behavior across cruise through post-flameout transonic/high-AoA flight with traceable aircraft-specific validation.
admission.release_condition: Obtain a distributable B777-200ER/Trent 892B aerodynamic, propulsion, actuator, and flight-control dataset with stated axes, units, configurations, uncertainty, and validation over the required envelope; or obtain permission to publish a reduced model and independent fixtures derived from such a dataset.
allowed_now: Use the Boeing/ATSB trajectory exports as external validation-only fixtures fetched by URL and hash.
Use the public point-mass polars only as explicitly named, non-admitted audit comparators.
Use certified Trent 892 identity and static LTO data as identity checks, not an in-flight or flameout thrust map.
forbidden_now: Do not install any audited family in the product estimator.
Do not splice OpenAP cruise drag, NASA generic high-AoA data, and FlightGear controls into a synthetic B777 model.
Do not force OpenAP's unlisted Trent 892 engine option and call the result a B777-200ER/Trent 892 model.
Do not infer priors from the candidate spread or tune any parameter to the 00:19 BFO or assumed impact.

admission_requirements.requirement: B777-200ER geometry, mass/inertia conventions, and Trent 892B-17 propulsion identity are explicit.
Lift, drag, and six-axis force/moment behavior cover attached cruise, transonic acceleration, stall onset, and post-stall high AoA with uncertainty.
Running, spool-down, flameout, windmilling drag, asymmetric thrust, and installation effects cover relevant Mach and altitude.
Surface authority/rates, hydraulic/electrical degradation, control-law transitions, TAC, autopilot and autothrottle disengagement are represented or explicitly conditioned.
Aircraft-specific fixtures exercise cruise trim, glide/energy behavior, transient loss of thrust, high-AoA motion, and time-step convergence.
Source/data redistribution and publication are permitted, with a pinned version, licence, source identity, and hashes.

candidate_families.name: OpenAP B772 point-mass drag and two-shaft thrust equations
candidate_families.model_identity: Generic ICAO B772 (777-200/200ER); current engine options omit Trent 892 and default to PW4090.
candidate_families.data_basis: Parabolic clean drag polar estimated from March 2018 Schiphol climb trajectories; simplified maximum/idle thrust performance equations.
blocking_findings: The B772 engine option list does not contain Trent 892; upstream raises an aircraft/engine mismatch unless force_engine is used.
The drag equations omit angle of attack, sideslip, angular rates, moments, and stall.
Idle thrust is defined as seven percent of modeled available thrust, not flameout or windmilling drag.

The paper's B772 coefficients (cd0=0.034, k=0.051, e=0.723) changed in commit 2ca2a05cc4c11fc7bff22f40f4098d06f229e62e to current values (0.024, 0.047, 0.783) without a cited B772 validation artifact in that change.
The paper's external aerodynamic validation example is a B747 model, not B772.

candidate_families.name: Community FlightGear YASim 777-200ER definitions
candidate_families.model_identity: Community 777-labelled geometry; historical file declares 93,400-lbf engines described as Trent 895, while the modern GPL file actively declares GE90-115B engines at 115,540 lbf.
candidate_families.data_basis: YASim geometry, solver targets, stall-shape knobs, engine scalars, and control mappings; no located aircraft-specific calibration report.
blocking_findings: Neither pinned definition is a Trent 892B-17 model.
The modern redistributable definition activates a GE90-115B, an engine/airframe mismatch for this scope.
The historical definition lacks a located repository-root or file-level licence at the pinned commit.
No primary calibration, uncertainty, or B777 flight-validation artifact was located for the aerodynamic or control parameters.

candidate_families.name: Official JSBSim model inventory
candidate_families.model_identity: No B777, B772, or Trent 892 model is present in the pinned official release.
candidate_families.data_basis: General-purpose six-degree-of-freedom simulation framework and bundled example aircraft.
blocking_findings: A capable simulation framework is not an aerodynamic dataset.
The official v1.3.1 archive contains no B777/Trent 892 aircraft-engine family to audit.

candidate_families.name: ATSB/Boeing engineering-simulator end-of-flight cases
candidate_families.model_identity: B777 engineering simulator; ATSB states the aerodynamic model was the same as a Level D simulator, while Boeing cautioned that some trajectories left the validated database.
candidate_families.data_basis: Ten one-second X, Y, altitude exports; requested initial ranges and electrical scenarios are described only in aggregate.
blocking_findings: The simulator model, equations, coefficients, complete initial conditions, control states, atmosphere, and uncertainty were not released.
Legal restrictions prevented ATSB from providing detailed per-case conditions.
ATSB permission covered sharing the exports on Iannello's blog; no general downstream licence was located.
The final CSV records remain above sea level and therefore are trajectory extracts, not complete impact solutions.

candidate_families.name: NASA Generic Transport / Transport Class Model
candidate_families.model_identity: Generic mid-weight twin-jet transport, not a B777.
candidate_families.data_basis: Scaled wind-tunnel-derived nonlinear tables covering alpha -5 to 85 degrees and beta +/-45 degrees, representative hydraulic actuators, and generic 40,000-lbf engines.
blocking_findings: Geometry, inertia, engines, actuators, and aerodynamic tables are intentionally generic.
No public primary source provides a defensible transformation or uncertainty model from TCM to B777-200ER/Trent 892B.
Using the tables would require an invented cross-aircraft prior.

candidate_families.name: ICAO certified Trent 892 static emissions-test points
candidate_families.model_identity: Trent 892 certification family; 9M-MRO identity is separately reported as Trent 892B-17.
candidate_families.data_basis: Rated static thrust and four LTO fuel-flow points supplied by the manufacturer for emissions certification.
blocking_findings: Static certification points do not form an in-flight thrust model.
The generic Trent 892 row cannot establish all 892B-17 installation and post-flameout behavior.

candidate_families.name: EUROCONTROL BADA
candidate_families.model_identity: Potential B772 performance family, not acquired for this redistributable source audit.
candidate_families.data_basis: Licensed aircraft performance algorithms and manufacturer/manual-derived data.
blocking_findings: The official terms require a reviewed, non-transferable licence rather than permitting a public source package.
BADA is a performance model and is not evidence of post-stall six-degree-of-freedom B777 behavior.
